text.approach: I-90 Exit 34 near North Bend, then the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FR 56) past the Taylor River bridge junction to a pullout roughly 2.6 miles further on, by a gravel wash. From the car the whole route is only about 1.5 miles horizontally, but 4,400 vertical feet. Start up the dry creek bed and leave it partway up into the woods, following a mix of flagging tape and faint trail up steep pine-needle slopes — 'scrumbling', pulling on whatever vegetation is at hand. About an hour in, at roughly 2,200 ft, you reach the dirt gully. Note that the pine-needle slopes above the slab run about 40 degrees on loose duff; huckleberry stems make good handholds.

text.overview: The standard line to Garfield's true 5,519 ft summit and the one Beckey called 'a hazardous enigma': 4,400 feet of dirt gully, brush, slab and ledge navigation from the Middle Fork road to the Y Notch, then four or five pitches of loose, barely protectable low-5th climbing up #2 Gully to the summit slabs. Under two miles horizontally and a minimum of twelve hours.
text.descent: From the summit scramble down to the top of the easy slab and rig a single-rope rappel to the col at the top of #2 Gully.
